ra: Kuvava/Kybebe is the chief mother-goddess of the Lydian pantheon at Sardis (Munn 2006).
Santas/Sandon is a principal Lydian war/kingship god (Munn 2006).
Artimus is attested across the Lydian inscriptional pantheon (Munn 2006).
Pldans appears in Lydian inscriptions, often paired with Artimus.
Lametrus is an attested Lydian grain-goddess theonym.
Bakivalis reflects the Lydian Dionysiac/wine-cult sphere.
Kandaules is a Lydian divine epithet (Hermes-type guardian) within Sardian cult.
Artimus and Pldans recur together in Lydian protective inscription formulae, mirroring the Greek Artemis-Apollo pairing.
The Lydian Kuvava/Kybebe is a key link in the reception chain (Kubaba > Kuvava/Kybebe > Cybele) producing the Greek Cybele/Magna Mater (Munn 2006).
Lydian Kuvava continues the name and figure of the Luwian/Neo-Hittite Kubaba of Carchemish.
Lydian Santas is the western-Anatolian continuation of the Luwian war/plague god Santa (ancestor of Cilician Sandas).
Greeks interpreted the club-bearing Lydian Santas/Sandon as Heracles, grounding the Heraclid dynasty of Sardis (interpretatio Graeca; Munn 2006).
Lydian Artimus is the local form regularly equated with Greek Artemis on phonetic and functional grounds.
Pldans is conventionally identified with Greek Apollo by name and protective/oracular function.
Lydian Lametrus is identified with Greek Demeter by name and agrarian grain function.
The Lydian Baki- wine/ecstatic cult is syncretized with Dionysus, who carries the Lydian-derived epithet Bakchos.
Hipponax reports Kandaules ('dog-throttler') as a Lydian title of Hermes, a guardian/psychopomp figure.
